data.summary: The plan tackles the weak units first, then cycles through the remaining units, ending with a mixed review week. Each week’s tasks are concrete, single‑sitting activities that fit the 5‑hour limit.

tasks: Do 20 practice problems on 1.1 and 1.2, marking each answer
Create a motion‑graph worksheet for 1.3 and solve it
Attend live class 10000
After class, solve 15 problems on impulse and momentum change
Work through 10 collision problems (elastic and inelastic)
Write a short summary of conservation of momentum principles
Complete 12 torque‑kinematics problems
Draw free‑body diagrams for a rotating system
Attend live class 10001
Post‑class, solve 10 problems on torque and rotational inertia

weeks.focus: Energy and momentum of rotating systems
tasks: Solve 8 problems on rotational kinetic energy and torque work
Create a concept map linking energy and momentum in rotation
Do 10 practice problems on SHM frequency and period
Sketch displacement‑time graphs for two oscillators
Solve 10 problems on density and pressure calculations
Explain how pressure varies with depth in a fluid
Take a timed practice quiz covering all listed topics
Review incorrect answers and note key concepts
Complete a full-length AP Physics 1 practice exam under timed conditions
Analyze performance and create a brief action plan for weak areas

data.final_week_advice: Use week 10 to simulate exam conditions, then focus on any remaining weak spots before the actual test.
